title: Why 3f + 1 and not 2f + 1
request:
One Byzantine fault, first with three nodes and then with four

./your_program.sh byzantine
init 3 1
safe
intersect
init 4 1
safe
intersect
note: With three nodes and one liar, a quorum would have to be all three — and then nothing is available while one node is merely slow. Four is the first size where a quorum is both reachable and guaranteed to overlap another quorum in an honest node.

title: What a client may believe
request:
Three replies that mostly agree, then three that do not

./your_program.sh byzantine
init 4 1
decide red red blue
decide red blue green
note: Two matching replies with f = 1 means at least one honest node said it, which is enough. Three different answers means at most one of them came from an honest node and there is no way to tell which — so the client must wait for more replies rather than pick the most popular.
